sections.heading: The near future: aller + infinitive
sections.body:
The easiest way to talk about the future is *aller* (present) + an infinitive — just like English "going to":

- *Je vais partir en vacances.* — I'm going to go on holiday.
- *Tu vas venir ce soir ?* — Are you going to come tonight?
- *Il va pleuvoir.* — It's going to rain.
- *Nous allons visiter Paris.* — We're going to visit Paris.
- *Ils vont se marier.* — They're going to get married.

Negative: *ne… pas* goes around *aller*: *Je ne vais pas travailler demain.*

sections.heading: When? Time expressions for the future
sections.body:
*ce soir* (tonight), *demain* (tomorrow), *après-demain* (the day after tomorrow), *ce week-end*, *la semaine prochaine* (next week), *le mois prochain*, *l'année prochaine*, *dans deux jours* (in two days' time), *bientôt* (soon), *plus tard* (later).

*Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ce week-end ? — Je vais voir des amis et je vais faire du sport.*

sections.heading: Talking about plans
sections.body:
- *J'ai envie de…* — I feel like…: *J'ai envie de voyager.*
- *J'ai l'intention de…* — I intend to…
- *Je compte…* — I'm planning to…: *Je compte partir en juin.*
- *Mon projet, c'est de…* — My plan is to…: *Mon projet, c'est d'apprendre le français.*

sections.heading: Pronunciation: linking words
sections.body:
French links words together in speech so that a sentence flows like one long word:

- **Enchaînement** — a pronounced final consonant runs into the next vowel: *il arrive* /i.la.ʁiv/, *elle aime* /ɛ.lɛm/.
- **Elision** — a final vowel disappears before another vowel, and the spelling shows it: *je + aime* → *j'aime*; *le + ami* → *l'ami*; *que + il* → *qu'il*.
- **Liaison** — a normally silent final consonant is pronounced before a vowel: *vous allez* /vu.z‿a.le/, *nous allons*, *ils ont*, *un ami* /œ̃.n‿a.mi/, *les enfants*, *deux ans* /dø.z‿ɑ̃/, *très important* /tʁɛ.z‿ɛ̃.pɔʁ.tɑ̃/.

Liaison is required after *les, des, un, mon, nous, vous, ils, elles* and before a noun or verb starting with a vowel. You'll learn exactly when it is required, optional or forbidden at A2.

examples: Je vais partir en vacances.
I'm going to go on holiday.
Tu vas venir ce soir ?
Are you going to come tonight?
Il va pleuvoir cet après-midi.
It's going to rain this afternoon.
Nous allons visiter Paris le mois prochain.
We're going to visit Paris next month.
Ils vont se marier l'année prochaine.
They're going to get married next year.
Je ne vais pas travailler demain.
I'm not going to work tomorrow.
Qu'est-ce que tu vas faire ce week-end ?
What are you going to do this weekend?
Je vais voir des amis.
I'm going to see some friends.
J'ai envie de voyager.
I feel like travelling.
Mon projet, c'est d'apprendre le français.
My plan is to learn French.
On se voit dans deux jours !
See you in two days!
Elle va arriver bientôt.
She's going to arrive soon.
Vous allez aimer ce film.
You're going to like this film.
